claims.text: In a release build, when a widget's build throws, Flutter shows a gray area (ErrorWidget's default in release) in place of the failed widget, and the rest of the app keeps running.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs, Handling errors in Flutter (testing/errors): ErrorWidget.builder default, debug red / release gray background; app-experience.md lines 15-17 @ stage-4

claims.text: Flutter routes errors it catches during build, layout and paint (and other framework callbacks) to FlutterError.onError; errors Flutter does not catch itself, such as from an async call started by a button's onPressed, go to PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs, Handling errors in Flutter: intro, 'Errors not caught by Flutter'

claims.text: By default FlutterError.onError calls FlutterError.presentError, which dumps the error to the device logs; the PlatformDispatcher error callback by default only prints errors. Both handlers are typically set in main().
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs, Handling errors in Flutter: paragraphs on FlutterError.onError default, PlatformDispatcher default, 'set them in your void main()'

claims.text: At stage-4 no file under DonHang.App/lib sets FlutterError.onError or PlatformDispatcher; grep -rnE "FlutterError\.onError|PlatformDispatcher" DonHang.App/lib docs/design prints only app-experience.md lines 37 and 38.

app-experience.md: lab measurement = profile mode on the team's machine plus bundle size via scripts/frontend/web-bundle.sh; these say nothing about customers' phones, browsers and networks; on-device errors may never reach the server.

app-experience.md table: A1 crash-free sessions, 99.5% of sessions over 28 days; A2 time from page load start to first screen on the customer's browser, p75 < 3 s, p95 < 6 s; A3 orders in the offline queue not at the API 30 min after placing, < 0.1% of orders; all targets assumed.

app-experience.md: S1-S4 in slo.md measure requests that reached the API, A1-A3 what happens before, on the device; an order stuck in the queue never becomes a failed request in S1; targets are reset after the first 28 days of real numbers.

Planned collection: both handlers set in main.dart, recording the error in the current session then letting Flutter handle it as before; a session = one app opening with a random id not tied to the customer; on page close/hide one report (error?, time to first screen, queued orders, oldest age).

Reports would go to a new public API endpoint needing its own rate limit since anyone can call it; at stage-4 nothing is collected, no endpoint exists, Program.cs limits are unchanged, and server SLIs in slo.md are the only numbers watched.
slo.md's SLIs count only requests that reach DonHang.Api; at stage-4 production has no Prometheus, while staging has Prometheus scraping the api Pods, so SLIs are measured on staging only.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/slo.md @ stage-4 lines 8-18, 106-107 (Chưa có: Prometheus trên production)

claims.text: Crash-free sessions counts a session with any uncaught error as failed, including a gray area where the app never closed; lab measurements find slow code but cannot stand in for customers' devices.

When only one measure fits, start with A1 errors; keep the report endpoint closed until it has a rate limit; a larger bundle is a lab signal of direction, only A2 shows whether customers' percentiles moved.
